I'm on the algorithm team working on our NPU inference pipeline. The BSP team keeps telling me there's 'insufficient compute bandwidth' for our model but I don't understand what that means in hardware terms. Our model needs 15 TOPS for real-time inference at 30fps, and the NPU spec says it supports 20 TOPS. So why is it slow?

Our model profile:
  - ResNet-50 backbone: 4.1 GFLOPs per frame
  - Custom detection head: 2.3 GFLOPs per frame
  - Total: 6.4 GFLOPs per frame @ 30fps = 192 GFLOPs/s
  - Model weights: 98MB (INT8 quantized)
  - Activation memory peak: 24MB
  - Batch size: 1

The BSP team mentioned 'memory bandwidth bottleneck' and 'Roofline model' but I need these concepts explained in terms I can relate to my algorithm work.
